short: A decisive Athenian victory over invading Persian forces, halting the first Persian invasion of Greece.
full:
In 490 BCE, an invading Persian army sent by King Darius I landed at the bay of Marathon, intending to subjugate Athens for supporting the Ionian Revolt. Despite being significantly outnumbered, the Athenian infantry, supported by a small contingent from Plataea, launched a surprise rapid advance against the Persian lines, crushing their flanks and routing the centre.

The victory shattered the myth of Persian invincibility and secured Athenian independence. It proved a defining moment for classical Greek culture and gave rise to the legendary run of Pheidippides to Athens to announce the victory.
